testcase.description: The names of the cocotb test cases to run for this design. The flow setting `cocotb.testcase` overrides them.
testcase.title: Testcase

always_runs.description: Run this generator on every launch: what it reads cannot be judged (it is not files, or they cannot be listed), so Xeda keeps no record that could show its output to be current. A generator that declares no `sources` runs on every launch anyway.
always_runs.title: Always Runs

args.description: The arguments the executable is run with: a list, or one string split on whitespace (as `command` is).
args.title: Args

class.description: The class of the generator. Without it, the table is a plain generator that runs `command`, `executable` or `shell`.

generated_sources.description: The entries of `rtl.sources` that this generator produces, when it produces only some of them. An entry names one of them, or a directory that holds some. Empty, every entry of `rtl.sources` is the generator's. An entry of `rtl.sources` is wholly the generator's or wholly written by hand: a pattern that would match both is an error. A generator's entry is a path (or a pattern) below the design root that the generator writes, or `$XEDA_GENERATED/<name>` for a file in the storage of the generator. An item selects the entries of its own kind. `$XEDA_GENERATED` alone selects every storage entry, and a storage entry that no item selects is an error.
generated_sources.title: Generated Sources

outputs_to.description: A directory that receives a copy of the generated sources, each under its path (a tree entry `gen/top.v` goes to `<outputs_to>/gen/top.v`) or under its name in the storage of the generator (`$XEDA_GENERATED/gen/top.v` goes to the same place). A copy onto a tree entry is refused, since the next run would read it. Give a location: an absolute path, or a path below `$DESIGN_ROOT`, `$DESIGN_DIR` or `$PWD`. The copy is made at the end of a launch that passed, as every delivery is (`--overwrite-outputs` replaces a changed copy). The flows never read the copy, and it is no part of any identity.
outputs_to.title: Outputs To

shell.description: A command line that a shell runs, such as `python soc.py --build`. Xeda expands nothing in it: the shell does. `shell` excludes `command` and `executable`.
shell.title: Shell

sources.description: The sources this generator reads, as a design's `sources` name them: a path relative to the design root, or a pattern where `*` is the only pattern character. Each one's content is what decides whether the generator runs again, so each has to exist. A directory counts as every file in it, so name what the generator reads from outside the design too (a library tree, an editable clone). Xeda assumes nothing about the generator's language or environment.
sources.title: Sources

standard.description: The version of the language standard.
standard.title: Standard

Rtl.description: The RTL: sources, top module, clocks, generator, attributes, parameters and defines.

attributes.description:
HDL attributes for modules, ports and other objects. The flow that reads an attribute
        decides its meaning and behavior.
        Write the attributes as a mapping of attr_name->(path->attr_value):
        - the key is the name of the attribute
        - the value is a mapping of path->attr_value:
            - the key is the path or scope on which the attribute applies
            - the value is the value of the attribute
attributes.title: Attributes

clock.description: Single design clock shorthand. Prefer an object with `port`. `null` means no clock.

defines.description: Verilog preprocessor macros, as a mapping of macro name to value. A value of `null` defines the macro without a value.

sources.description: Source files, in compile order: a path relative to the design root (`$DESIGN_ROOT` and `$DESIGN_DIR` name it too), or a table, in YAML `{file: ..., type: ...}` (`path` in place of `file` for one not written yet). A path containing `*` is a pattern: its files are inserted in sorted order, and it must match at least one. `*` is the only pattern character: `?`, `[` and `]` are part of a file name, so `rtl/fifo[1].v` names exactly that file. In `rtl.sources` of a design with a generator, an entry that the generator writes is a path below the design root (it need not exist yet), or `$XEDA_GENERATED/<name>` for a file in the storage of the generator.
sources.title: Sources

targets.description: Named targets (for example, one per board), each an overlay on the design: it takes the design's own keys, merged over them. Mappings merge key by key; `sources` are appended after the design's; any other list replaces the design's. One is selected with `--target NAME`; without it, the design is used with no target. A target name cannot be the name of a flow.
